newsitem.title: FRANCE: Major sees solution in Franco-US spat over NATO.
newsitem.headline: Major sees solution in Franco-US spat over NATO.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said in an interview published in Paris on Monday he believed a settlement would be found to a Franco-American spat over control of NATO commands.
"I believe a solution that will adddress our common main aims will be found," Major told the newspaper Le Figaro.
"The future (NATO command) structure will have to be efficient militarily. It will have to address European aspirations but also have wide political support in the United States.

"It will have to express a coherent and visible European identity with new tasks and even more influence (devolved to Europeans). I strongly hope France will fully regain its place in NATO because both France and Europe will gain from this," he said.

Paris and Washington have been deadlocked for several months over a French demand that a European officer take over NATO's southern command as part of a drive to give European nations greater responsibility for their own defence.
The Naples-based command controls allied forces in the Mediterranean including Bosnia.
Britain has taken a cautious stand in the dispute though French officials say London ultimately backs Washington's position.
French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Sunday Paris might fail to persuade Washington to let a European take over the Naples command from an American.
Washington last week publicly rejected a French compromise proposal to split the command, giving a U.S. admiral control over air-naval protection forces and a European territorial responsibility.
France, planning to make a full return to NATO's military command which it quit in 1966, wants European nations given a greater responsibility for their own defence.
In September, French Defence Minister Charles Millon threatened to freeze France's reintegration into NATO's military structure if it failed to get its way. Officials have not repeated that threat.
